rationale: Any authenticated user could call DELETE /api/v1/sources and delete all sources, agents and assessments of all customers; no per-user filtering or authorization. Fix removes the operation.
CoAP request query parameters injected as Camel headers (header injection to command execution); not an access-control decision on an HTTP operation.
Plugin route action check was not scoped to the datasource, so a user holding the action on any other data source passed the check for a data source whose route required that action.
A user with READ on one exact key opened a Watch with an open-ended range and received events for all keys at or above it; range normalization ran before the permission check.
With prompt=none and empty scope, consent was checked against an empty set, so a client got a token with all registered scopes though the user consented to a subset. Contract entry is deprecated.
After an admin revoked a user's permission to mint service account tokens, the stale permission cache let the user still mint tokens for a few seconds. Fix clears the cache on permission change.
A worker of tenant A could register another tenant's durable task id on its stream and receive that tenant's callback payload; routing was keyed by task id only. Interface is gRPC, not in contract.
A user with access to an application could get, modify, delete, act on, read logs or events of resources on the destination cluster outside the application and project permissions.
updateUser did not compare the target username to the caller, so a non-admin user could update another user's data including password; a non-admin could also set isadmin.
System API routes were installed on the party without the JWT and auth handlers, so they could be called without credentials. Fix moves them under the authenticated party.
In multi-user mode, any authenticated user could modify or delete shared pipelines (empty namespace) because authorization was skipped for write operations.
Job routes lacked JWT and RBAC middleware, so an unauthenticated caller could list, create, read, modify and delete jobs.
Admission plugin treated a missing service account identity as authorized for every PodSecurityPolicy, so a user could create pods under any policy. Contract security block truncated.

API Builder object entry reads ran with the permission checker of the object definition owner, so guest users could read object entries. Fix removes the override. Endpoints are dynamic and not in contract.
Any authenticated CalDAV user knowing a task UID could read the task of another user's project; project in the URL was ignored and no access check was done. CalDAV not in contract.
The SCIM endpoint handler served requests without requiring an admin, so callers lacking admin rights could use SCIM user creation. Fix adds RequireAdmin. Caller identity before fix unclear.
